# Results -- Study 281 (El-Nino) on ^GSPC and USO

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). NOAA ONI (NDJ season,
1950-2024) is hardcoded in [`data.py`](../el_nino/data.py); ^GSPC and USO daily
closes are read cache-only from the repo-level `_cache`. Match the fingerprints
below to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC (nominal price, Dec/Dec), ENSO lag-1 | 1951-2025 | 75 years | `57cb2623acd8` |
| USO (crude-oil ETF, Dec/Dec), ENSO lag-1 | 2007-2025 | 19 years | `0f315807ecb3` |
| NOAA ONI (NDJ) | Winters 1950-2024 | 75 winters | hardcoded constant |

ENSO phase mix (ONI +/-0.5 threshold, lag-1 equity window): **26 El Nino,
29 La Nina, 20 Neutral**.

## The honest baseline -- the key number

The S&P 500 rose in **55 of 75** lag-1 years: **unconditional up-rate = 73.3%**,
mean annual return **+9.4%**. Equities drift up regardless of the ocean; any
"El-Nino-is-bullish" rule inherits that drift for free. The correct test is whether
El Nino years beat La Nina years by more than sampling noise -- not whether El Nino
years are merely positive.

## Equity signal (^GSPC, lag-1) -- the primary spec

| Phase | n years | mean annual return |
|---|--:|--:|
| El Nino | 26 | **+11.9%** |
| La Nina | 29 | **+8.8%** |
| Neutral | 20 | **+7.1%** |
| All years (baseline) | 75 | **+9.4%** |

- **El-Nino-minus-La-Nina gap: +3.2pp.** Sits on top of ~17% annual volatility with
  ~25-29 obs per phase -- exactly the size of gap chance produces when 75 noisy years
  are sliced three ways.
- **Welch t (El Nino vs La Nina returns): t = +0.692**, p = 0.492 -- far below |t| = 2.
- **One-way ANOVA (three phases): F = 0.508, p = 0.604** -- phase explains essentially
  none of the year-to-year variance.
- **Permutation p (|gap|, 10,000 shuffles): p = 0.480** -- the observed gap is an
  ordinary draw from the null; ~half of random label-shuffles produce a bigger gap.
- **Newey-West HAC t on the long-short series: t = +0.441** -- the long-short premium
  is statistically zero. This is the number that pins the Signal axis at NONE.

## Sub-periods / robustness (degrees of freedom)

| Tape | n | El-La gap | Welch t | perm p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Equity, lag-1 (primary) | 75 | +3.2pp | +0.69 | 0.480 |
| Equity, lag-0 (contemporaneous) | 75 | +1.95pp | +0.42 | 0.649 |
| Oil (USO), lag-1 | 19 | -3.1pp | -0.16 | 0.859 |

The lag-0 (contemporaneous) join is even weaker, and the commodity tape -- where the
folklore is loudest -- has the **wrong sign**: oil averaged **-2.2%** in El Nino years
vs **+0.9%** in La Nina years (perm p = 0.859, n = 19). The much-touted drought-spike
channel is absent (indeed reversed) in the tradable oil ETF.

## Could you trade it? -- net of costs and borrow

Long S&P after an El Nino winter, short after a La Nina winter, one-year lag, 10bps
one-way costs, 50bps annual borrow on the shorts (turnover ~1.0 round-trip/yr):

| Strategy | Annualised |
|---|--:|
| ENSO long-short, gross | **-0.6%/yr** |
| ENSO long-short, net of costs + borrow | **-0.9%/yr** |
| Buy & hold S&P | **+8.1%/yr** |

The long-short *loses* money because La Nina years were not bear years -- they
averaged +8.8% -- and shorting them throws away the equity risk premium.

## The n ~ 25/phase power wall

With ~25 obs per phase and ~17% equity volatility, the minimum detectable El-La mean
gap at 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05, is:

    MDE = (t_crit + t_power) * 0.17 * sqrt(2/25) ~= 7%/yr

The observed +3.2pp gap is **less than half** the detectable threshold. Even if the
gap were real, we would need roughly twice the available ENSO history to resolve it.

## Positive control

On a synthetic tape (n = 600) the engine recovers a planted El Nino premium once it
is large enough: a 500 bps/yr premium yields Welch t ~ 4.9 and permutation p < 0.001;
a 0 bps null yields a non-significant gap. The machinery works -- the real tape simply
has no signal to find.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Equity gap +3.2pp, Welch t = 0.69, HAC t = 0.44, ANOVA p = 0.60,
  perm p = 0.48; oil gap -3.1pp (wrong sign), perm p = 0.86. No tape clears the
  desk's robust HAC |t| >= 2 bar. n ~ 25/phase is too small to detect anything less
  than a ~7%/yr structural premium, and there isn't one.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The long-short strategy underperforms buy-and-hold
  (gross -0.6%/yr vs +8.1%/yr) before borrow costs; shorting La Nina years discards
  the equity premium. There is no tradable edge.
- **Busted -- a real weather effect that never reaches the tape.** ENSO genuinely
  shifts global weather and spot commodity prices (Cashin et al. 2017), but the
  effect does not transmit to forecastable, tradable equity or oil-ETF returns -- and
  in our oil sample it went the *opposite* way to the folklore.
